source: Cambodia Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ តាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" [System of Rice Intensification Following Natural Principles / SRI], 14-page Khmer-language handout/booklet, undated, no author or elibrary URL visible on any page (footer reads "កំរណ៉ការអភិវ័ទ្ធន៍វិស្ស័យកសិកម្ម ខែត្តកំពងចាម" = "Agricultural Extension/Skills Development Office, Kampong Cham province")
text:
The System of Rice Intensification (SRI), called in Khmer the rice cultivation system following natural principles (ប.វ.ស), is presented to farmers with a list of expected practical benefits: seedlings germinate well; nursery seedlings can be ready for transplanting at 8-10 days (very young, per the crop-duration diagram on the same page); plants produce many tillers, reportedly 50-60 stems per hill; plants develop many long roots; panicles are large and numerous; the milled rice has good eating quality/taste; and the method reduces environmental pollution.

Stated quality/performance claims for SRI, based on farm-level experience described in the source: SRI can raise rice yield by roughly 2 to 3 times compared to normal (conventional) practice; it reduces the cost of chemical fertilizer; it reduces the cost of pesticide and herbicide use; and it helps preserve soil fertility and reduces negative impact on the environment for future generations.

The document frames rice growth as three main cycles/stages: a growth (vegetative) cycle, whose duration varies according to variety duration class (short/early, medium, or long/late maturing varieties); a yield-formation (reproductive) cycle lasting about 35 days; and a ripening cycle lasting about 30 days. Within the growth cycle farmers are told to focus on seed preparation, seed quality checking, seedbed preparation and sowing, choice of irrigation method, seedling care, fertilizing, and general crop care; within the yield-formation cycle, on maintaining good water levels, keeping the soil aerated, and controlling pests and rats; within the ripening cycle, on watching for problems such as lodging, birds, and correct harvest timing. This three-stage/ten-numbered-substage growth framework overlaps with the existing rice_morphology_growth_stages KB topic and was not re-extracted in full detail here.
